short_description: A crunch variation with arms crossed over the chest that targets the rectus abdominis.
how_to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Cross your arms over your chest.
Exhale and curl your upper back off the floor.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower with control.
correct: Keep your lower back controlled.
Keep your chin lifted off your chest.
Move slowly and with control.
Keep your feet flat on the floor.
mistakes: Don't let your feet lift off the floor.

short_description: A crunch with arms extended overhead that increases the lever length and challenges the abs more deeply.
how_to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Extend your arms straight overhead close to your ears.
Exhale and curl your shoulders off the floor.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly.
correct: Keep your lower back controlled.
Keep your arms in line with your ears.
Move at a steady, controlled pace.
Keep your core tight throughout.
mistakes: Don't let your arms drift out to the sides.

short_description: A foundational isometric hold that builds core, shoulder and back stability.
how_to: Place your forearms on the floor with elbows under your shoulders.
Extend your legs back and rest on your toes.
Brace your core and align your body in a straight line.
Hold the position and breathe steadily.
correct: Keep your body in one line.
Keep your core engaged.
Keep your hips level.
Breathe steadily throughout.
mistakes: Don't let your lower back sag.
Don't lift your hips too high.

short_description: A seated rotation exercise that works the obliques and deep core muscles.
how_to: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and heels slightly raised.
Lean back slightly to engage your core.
Clasp your hands together in front of you.
Rotate your torso to one side, then the other, in a controlled rhythm.
correct: Keep your chest tall throughout.
Keep your core braced as you rotate.
Move from your torso, not just your arms.
Keep your heels low if needed for balance.
mistakes: Don't twist with just your arms.
Don't let your hips shift with each rotation.

short_description: A marching drill that raises the knees high to warm up the hips and elevate the heart rate.
how_to: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Drive one knee up toward your chest.
Lower it and immediately drive the other knee up.
Pump your arms in opposition to your legs.
correct: Keep your chest tall and upright.
Drive your knees up deliberately.
Keep a steady rhythm.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.
mistakes: Don't lean back as your knees come up.
Don't let your arms hang limp.
Don't shuffle your feet — lift them clearly.

short_description: A crunch variation where the body folds into a V shape to engage the full abdominal wall.
how_to: Lie flat on your back with your arms extended overhead.
In one motion, lift your legs and upper back off the floor.
Reach your hands toward your feet at the top.
Lower slowly and return to the starting position.
correct: Keep your lower back controlled.
Keep the movement smooth and controlled.
Keep your legs straight as they rise.
Breathe out as you fold up.
mistakes: Don't slam your back down on the way back.
Don't bend your knees to make it easier than intended.

short_description: A side-to-side crunch variation that targets the obliques by reaching toward each heel.
how_to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Lift your head and shoulders slightly off the floor.
Reach your right hand to your right heel by side-bending right.
Return to center and repeat on the left side.
correct: Keep your lower back pressed gently into the floor.
Keep your neck relaxed, not strained.
Control the side bend — don't flop.
Keep your feet flat throughout.
mistakes: Don't lift your hips to reach farther.

short_description: A standing variation of the bicycle crunch that works the obliques and challenges balance.
how_to: Stand tall with your hands lightly behind your head.
Drive your right knee up while twisting your left elbow toward it.
Lower and switch, bringing your left knee up to your right elbow.
Alternate sides in a steady rhythm.
correct: Keep your lower back controlled.
Keep your chest open — don't collapse forward.
Rotate from your torso, not just your arms.
Keep a soft bend in your standing knee.
mistakes: Don't just tap the elbow to the knee — rotate fully.
Don't lean forward from the hips.

short_description: A supine spinal rotation stretch that releases tension in the lower back and hips.
how_to: Lie on your back with your arms out to your sides.
Bend one knee and bring it across your body toward the floor.
Keep your shoulder blades flat on the floor.
Hold the twist and breathe, then switch sides.
correct: Keep your shoulders grounded throughout.
Breathe steadily into the stretch.
Keep the movement gentle and unhurried.
Relax your neck and jaw.
mistakes: Don't force the knee to the floor.
Don't lift your opposite shoulder off the floor.

short_description: A supine core stability exercise that trains the abs to resist extension as opposite limbs move.
how_to: Lie on your back with your arms pointing up and your knees bent at ninety degrees.
Press your lower back gently into the floor.
Lower your right arm overhead and your left leg toward the floor simultaneously.
Return to the start and repeat on the opposite side.
correct: Keep your lower back pressed into the floor throughout.
Keep your core braced as the limbs move.
Move slowly and with full control.
Breathe out as you extend.
mistakes: Don't let your lower back arch away from the floor.
Don't rush — slow movement is the point.
Don't let your limbs drop instead of lowering with control.
